static_traits.name: Pan Meilin
static_traits.social_status: Has some friends at school, but Avoiding socializing with classmates due to feeling intellectually inferior, and has not yet told friends about academic troubles and inferiority
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems or psychotherapy history in the past; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic, able to self-reflect and cooperate in exploration; open attitude toward problems, stable emotions and high cooperativeness

basic_info.main_problem: The problem I want to discuss is that, because I got a very poor grade in a university physics course, I am experiencing inferiority and low self-esteem. These feelings began after receiving the grade last semester. I believe the reason is that I think I lack intelligence.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling after realizing that these negative thoughts and feelings were affecting my learning motivation, academic performance, and overall well-being.
growth_experiences: Last semester received unsatisfactory grades in university physics, after which Self-doubt and low self-esteem began appearing frequently, thinking 'I am too stupid to learn'. Worsens when facing academic challenges or receiving feedback; tried studying harder and asking classmates for help, but the subjective inferiority and inadequacy persist. Also experiencing Social withdrawal (avoiding interaction with classmates) and sleep and eating rhythms disrupted by worry.

core_beliefs: I am not smart enough/I am stupid
I am not fit for university (one failure means everything is not working)

special_situations.event: Received unsatisfactory physics grades last semester
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one exam grade is poor, it proves I am not smart enough and not fit for university
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Proving myself and making up for inadequacies by studying twice as hard and asking classmates for help
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am too stupid; I cannot learn

special_situations.event: Facing new academic challenges or receiving assignment/exam feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot get it right the first time, it means I am not smart enough and will keep failing
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly self-criticizing, lowering expectations and motivation to avoid the blow of failing again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter how hard I try, the results will not be good

special_situations.event: Comparing with classmates in class or studying, seeing others understand faster or perform better
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others learn faster than me, it means I am very stupid and not as good as others
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding interaction with classmates, participating less in discussions to avoid revealing inadequacies
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are much smarter than me; I am not fit for university

special_situations.event: Preparing to communicate with classmates about studies or talk about one's feelings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I show not understanding or express vulnerability, I will be looked down upon and judged
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Choosing Silence and avoidance, not confiding in friends to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am stupid/look down on me

core_conflict.wish: Desiring to be seen as capable, accepted and recognized (as a qualified University student)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as stupid, Being rejected or feeling ashamed
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being judged by keeping distance and avoiding exposing inadequacies
Maintains a sense of control over the sense of worth through doubled effort and self-blame

object_relations.self_representation: A 'poor Student' not smart enough who may fail at any time
object_relations.object_representation: Smarter 'critics/judges' who judge oneself at any time (classmates, teachers, others)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Noticing others understand faster or perform better in class or classmate discussions, or worrying others will see my inadequacies
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to project inner 'Self-deprecation' onto others, experiencing it as 'they will look down on me and think I am stupid' (transference: treating others as judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using cautious, vague expressions, reducing self-disclosure; restrained tone, avoiding taking a clear stance, to lower the risk of being judged.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When receiving negative academic feedback or recalling failure experiences
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning Sense of frustration about external situations into total negation of and self-blame toward oneself ('it is all because I am not smart enough')
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tending to use self-blaming language (e.g. 'It is all my fault'), with a low tone, proactively magnifying personal faults and ignoring situational factors.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to talk about inner emotions or seek support from friends
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing that expressing vulnerability leads to Being rejected or being looked down upon, thus suppressing true emotions
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding briefly, downplaying feelings, avoiding emotional vocabulary; quickly turning the topic back to task or factual levels.

manifestations: Avoiding socializing with classmates due to feeling intellectually inferior
Not confiding academic Anxiety and inferiority to friends, bearing pressure alone
outcomes: Sleep and diet rhythms disrupted by worry
Impaired learning motivation and academic performance

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Believes classmates will think oneself is stupid and will judge oneself
Presetting negative evaluations before interacting with others, thus Withdrawing

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly blaming oneself: 'no matter how hard I try it is never good enough'
Overly cautious when expressing oneself; reduces self-disclosure

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Equates a single result with overall ability and self-worth
Treating 'good grades = smart = valuable' as an unquestionable standard

positive_force: Willing to study hard and once proactively sought academic help from classmates
Able to identify multiple possible influencing factors (Learning methods, exam Anxiety, etc.)
Willing to seek professional counseling and external resource support, positive attitude
negative_force: Globally negating based on one failure, over-binding self-worth to grades
Frequently comparing with others and belittling oneself accordingly
Anticipating future failure, mind-reading others' evaluations leading to Social avoidance
Self-reproach maintaining low self-esteem and Anxiety, further weakening motivation
Worrying about academic performance leading to Sleep and diet rhythm disturbance, affecting functional Recovery

target_behavior.behavior: Self-deprecation automatic thoughts (e.g. 'I am too stupid to learn')
antecedent: Seeing or recalling poor physics grades
target_behavior.core_reason: Globally attributing a single failure, and rigidly binding intelligence to self-worth to interpret uncertainty and Anxiety
target_behavior.function: Gaining a 'certain Interpretation' and short-term sense of control through self-blame, avoiding directly facing specific skill/method adjustments and uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Worsening Anxiety and low self-esteem, weakening Learning motivation and persistence, maintaining the failure-Anticipation and avoidance cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Social avoidance (reducing interaction with classmates/discussing academics)
antecedent: Class discussions or group collaboration situations
The moment of preparing to talk to classmates or friends about academic distress and feelings
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying that exposing inadequacies will be judged/looked down upon, producing shame and Fear of Being rejected
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the threat of being evaluated and the shame experience, briefly reducing Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Fewer opportunities to gain academic and emotional support, increased subjective sense of Loneliness, maintaining negative beliefs and functional impairment
